headline: What Is a
Treasury Yield,
and Why Does
Everyone Cite It?
slides.subtitle:
The most-quoted number in finance,
explained in 60 seconds.

slides.title: In One Sentence
slides.big: A Treasury yield is the annual return you earn for lending money to the U.S. government.
slides.body: It is quoted as a percentage, such as for 2-year or 10-year Treasuries.
slides.source: Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury

slides.title: How It Works
items: The Treasury sells bonds to raise money.
Investors bid, and the price settles.
Lower price means a higher yield.
slides.footer: Yield moves as bond prices change.
slides.disclaimer: For informational purposes only. Not investment advice.

slides.title: Why It Matters to You
slides.body: Treasury yields are a benchmark. Mortgage rates, car loans and savings rates often move in the same direction.

slides.title: Remember This
items: Yield is the return on lending to the U.S.
Price and yield move in opposite directions.
